title: Radial coordinates and extension of prescribed polytope boundary homeomorphisms
statement: Let $d,e\geq1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $Q\subset\mathbb R^e$ be bounded sets of the form $P=\{x:\ell_j(x)\leq a_j\ (j\in J)\}$ and $Q=\{y:m_k(y)\leq b_k\ (k\in K)\}$, where $J,K$ are finite sets, $\ell_j,m_k$ are nonzero real linear functionals, and $a_j,b_k$ are real numbers. Assume points $c\in\mathbb R^d$ and $v\in\mathbb R^e$ satisfy every corresponding inequality strictly. Use the usual Euclidean topologies, and subspace topologies on subsets [def-kun-subspace-topology]; write $\partial P=P\setminus\operatorname{int}P$ and $\partial Q=Q\setminus\operatorname{int}Q$. Each $x\in P\setminus\{c\}$ has unique coordinates $p\in\partial P$, $0<r\leq1$ with $x=c+r(p-c)$; both $p$ and $r$ depend continuously on $x$. The analogous assertion holds for $Q,v$. For every homeomorphism $\psi:\partial P\to\partial Q$, the map $H:P\to Q$ specified by $H(c)=v$ and $H(c+r(p-c))=v+r(\psi(p)-v)$ is a homeomorphism extending $\psi$. Its inverse is $v+r(q-v)\mapsto c+r(\psi^{-1}(q)-c)$, with $v\mapsto c$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary lemma expanding the coning/radial-extension input implicit in the boundary/horn-pair paragraph between Propositions 3.2.2 and 3.2.3, printed p.79 (PDF index 88). Hovey states the pairs but not this general extension lemma; no Stacks tag. General proof plan is in the worker report.

proof.text: Normalize the inequalities about $c$: put $\delta_j=a_j-\ell_j(c)>0$ and $f_j(w)=\ell_j(w)/\delta_j$. The index set $J$ is nonempty: otherwise $P=\mathbb R^d$, which is unbounded since $d\geq1$. Write $f_j(w)=\sum_{i=1}^d\alpha_{ji}w_i$ in standard coordinates, and set $A=1+\max_{j\in J}\sum_i|\alpha_{ji}|>0$. The triangle inequality and $|w_i-z_i|\leq\|w-z\|$ give $|f_j(w)-f_j(z)|\leq A\|w-z\|$ for every $j$. We use the subspace topologies defined in [def-kun-subspace-topology] throughout.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 1. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Define $g(w)=\max_{j\in J}f_j(w)$. For each $j$, $f_j(w)\leq f_j(z)+A\|w-z\|\leq g(z)+A\|w-z\|$; taking the maximum and interchanging $w,z$ gives $|g(w)-g(z)|\leq A\|w-z\|$. In particular $g$ is continuous, directly by this estimate. Linearity gives $g(0)=0$ and $g(tw)=t g(w)$ for every $t\geq0$ (also for $t=0$). Dividing each original inequality by its positive $\delta_j$ shows $c+w\in P$ if and only if $g(w)\leq1$. These are explicit finite-maximum and scalar calculations, not an invocation of a general gauge theorem.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 2. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: For $w\ne0$, one has $g(w)>0$. Indeed, if $g(w)\leq0$, then for every $t\geq0$, $g(tw)=t g(w)\leq0\leq1$, so $c+tw\in P$. This contradicts boundedness: $\|c+tw\|\geq t\|w\|-\|c\|$ tends to infinity because $\|w\|>0$. Thus $g$ vanishes only at $0$.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 3. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: The interior is exactly $\{c+w:g(w)<1\}$. If $g(w)<1$, the ball of radius $(1-g(w))/(2A)$ about $c+w$ lies in $P$, by the estimate in step 2. If $g(w)=1$, then $w\ne0$ and $g((1+t)w)=1+t>1$ for $t>0$; the points $c+(1+t)w$ lie outside $P$ and approach $c+w$. Hence such a point is not interior. Points with $g(w)>1$ do not belong to $P$, so cannot be interior. By the definition of boundary in the statement, $\partial P=\{c+w:g(w)=1\}$; in particular $c\notin\partial P$.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 4. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: For $x=c+w\in P\setminus\{c\}$ put $r(x)=g(w)$ and $p(x)=c+w/g(w)$. Steps 2 and 3 give $0<r(x)\leq1$. Positive homogeneity gives $g(p(x)-c)=g(w)/g(w)=1$, so step 4 puts $p(x)$ in $\partial P$. Substituting the definitions gives $x=c+r(x)(p(x)-c)$. Conversely, for $p\in\partial P$ and $0<r\leq1$, $g(r(p-c))=r$, so $c+r(p-c)$ belongs to $P\setminus\{c\}$.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 5. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: These coordinates are unique. If $x=c+s(u-c)$ with $u\in\partial P$ and $0<s\leq1$, step 4 gives $g(u-c)=1$; applying $g$ and its positive homogeneity gives $g(x-c)=s$. Consequently $s=r(x)$ and $u=c+(x-c)/s=p(x)$. This also shows that a boundary point has radial coordinates $(p,r)=(x,1)$.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 6. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Both coordinates are continuous on $P\setminus\{c\}$. The scalar coordinate is Lipschitz by step 2. For the boundary coordinate, fix $w_0\ne0$ and $\rho=g(w_0)>0$. If $\|w-w_0\|<\rho/(2A)$ then $g(w)>\rho/2$ and $|1/g(w)-1/\rho|\leq2A\|w-w_0\|/\rho^2$. Expanding $w/g(w)-w_0/\rho=(w-w_0)/g(w)+w_0(1/g(w)-1/\rho)$ bounds its norm by $(2/\rho+2A\|w_0\|/\rho^2)\|w-w_0\|$. This proves continuity into the ambient Euclidean space. Since $p(x)\in\partial P$, continuity into the subspace $\partial P$ follows directly from [def-kun-subspace-topology]: the inverse image of an open set $V\cap\partial P$ is the inverse image of $V$.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 7. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text:
Perform the same construction for $Q,v$, with $\epsilon_k=b_k-m_k(v)>0$, $h(z)=\max_{k\in K}m_k(z)/\epsilon_k$, and $B=1+\max_k\sum_i| eta_{ki}|$, where $m_k(z)/\epsilon_k=\sum_i eta_{ki}z_i$. Here $K
e\varnothing$ because $Q$ is bounded and $e\geq1$. Every calculation in steps 1–7 applies with these substitutions. In particular $h(tz)=t h(z)$ for $t\geq0$, $h(z)>0$ for $z
e0$, $|h(z)-h(z')|\leq B\|z-z'\|$, and the unique continuous coordinates are $s(y)=h(y-v)$ and $q(y)=v+(y-v)/s(y)$ for $y
e v$. Also $\partial Q=\{v+z:h(z)=1\}$.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 8. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Given the prescribed homeomorphism $\psi$, define $H(c)=v$ and $H(x)=v+r(x)(\psi(p(x))-v)$ for $x\ne c$. The point $\psi(p(x))$ belongs to $\partial Q$, so $h(H(x)-v)=r(x)h(\psi(p(x))-v)=r(x)\in(0,1]$. Thus $H(x)\in Q\setminus\{v\}$, with $Q$-coordinates $(\psi(p(x)),r(x))$. Similarly define $G(v)=c$ and $G(y)=c+s(y)(\psi^{-1}(q(y))-c)$ for $y\ne v$; it belongs to $P\setminus\{c\}$ and has $P$-coordinates $(\psi^{-1}(q(y)),s(y))$.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 9. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Using precisely the coordinates computed in step 9 gives $G(H(x))=c+r(x)(\psi^{-1}(\psi(p(x)))-c)=x$ for $x\ne c$, and $H(G(y))=v+s(y)(\psi(\psi^{-1}(q(y)))-v)=y$ for $y\ne v$. At the centers the two identities follow from the definitions. For $x\in\partial P$, step 6 gives $r(x)=1$ and $p(x)=x$, whence $H(x)=\psi(x)$. Thus the inverse and boundary restriction have exactly the formulas asserted in the statement.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 10. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Away from the centers, $H$ and $G$ are continuous: their formulas in step 9 are compositions of the continuous coordinates of steps 7–8, the given continuous maps $\psi,\psi^{-1}$, and vector addition and scalar multiplication in Euclidean spaces. These last operations are coordinatewise sums and products of real numbers. The restrictions to the punctured spaces suffice locally at every noncenter, since a ball of radius $\|x-c\|/2$ about $x\ne c$ avoids $c$, and likewise for $v$. Their images lie in $Q$ and $P$ respectively; [def-kun-subspace-topology] turns this ambient continuity into continuity for those codomains.

source.place: Agent supplement for the radial boundary-extension input below proof paragraph 2; explicit calculation, step 11. Context: Hovey, Model Categories, printed p.79, boundary/horn-pair paragraph; Hovey does not state this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: It remains to check continuity at the centers, without requiring a limit for the boundary coordinate. Boundedness supplies constants $M_P,M_Q\geq1$ with $\|p-c\|\leq M_P$ for all $p\in P$ and $\|q-v\|\leq M_Q$ for all $q\in Q$ (translate the given bounding balls and enlarge the radii). For $x\ne c$, $\|H(x)-v\|=r(x)\|\psi(p(x))-v\|\leq M_Q g(x-c)\leq M_Q A\|x-c\|$. This inequality also holds at $x=c$. Hence $\|x-c\|<\eta/(M_Q A)$ implies $\|H(x)-v\|<\eta$, for every $\eta>0$. Similarly $\|G(y)-c\|\leq M_P B\|y-v\|$, proving continuity at $v$. Together with steps 10–11, these estimates make $H$ a continuous bijection with continuous inverse $G$, which is the asserted homeomorphism.
